newsitem.title: GREECE: Blue chips drive Greek stocks 1.68 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips drive Greek stocks 1.68 pct higher.

text.p: Greek shares leaped 1.68 percent forward on Thursday after the market reported clear demand for banks, industrials and OTE telecom.
Fund managers said blue chips were favoured by a cocktail of positive news including a strong dollar and upbeat half-year profits and pointed out that the market's rise was not broadly-based.

"A large number of industrial stocks from the export-sector such as cement, aluminium and other metallurgicals were propped by the surge of the dollar in international markets," said Angelos Politis, fund manager at Helvetia mutual funds.
"The rise in prices is limited to blue chips, it is not across the board," he added.
The Athens general index jumped 1.68 percent or 25.92 points to the day's zenith of 1,569.15 from Wednesday's 1,543.23 close.
"Banks were led by Alpha Credit which the market expects it to post strong profit growth in its half-year statement," Politis said.
Alpha Credit is expected to announce its interim results later today.
